subject: Calculating sample level densities with cluster size as covariate

messages.author: 45906a28df896f54
messages.subject: Calculating sample level densities with cluster size as covariate
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I've run into a bit of a problem getting sample level density estimates from my point-count data and was wondering if anyone had any suggestions. I recently completed point count surveys at 150 points. The birds we're working with are fairly gregarious and have a high tendency to form flocks. As such, I expected that cluster size would be an important covariate for detection. After truncation, binning, etc it's clear that this is the case as all 5 of my top models are MCDS which include cluster size as a covariate.

My problem is that I'm also interested in then environmental relationships with density as well, and need to pull out point-specific density estimates in order to investigate them. I know that MCDS cannot produce sample level estimates of density when cluster size is used as a covariate, and found a great posting from a few years back explaining why this is, but couldn't find any suggestions for what to do about it...

The data, biology of the system, and basic logic all tell me that I need to include cluster size as a covariate, but I also need to calculate sample level density estimates. Is there any way to estimate sample level densities with cluster size as a covariate? Would using the R packages make doing so possible? If so how different would my density estimates/model selection be given thatnthe R packages use slightly different likelihood estimation? Lastly, if even the R packages can't get sample level density estimates, does anyone have any suggestions for how I should handle this?

Thanks for any and all help, I really appreciate it.

Best,
Nathaniel Behl
